root_cause.text: The `rpcrdma_post_recvs()` function increments `ep->re_receiving` at the start but fails to decrement it on early exit paths (when `atomic_inc_return()` returns > 1 or when no work requests are available), causing the counter to never reach zero and blocking `rpcrdma_xprt_drain()` indefinitely.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes two early `goto out;` statements to `goto out_dec;`, which now unconditionally executes `atomic_dec_return(&ep->re_receiving)` before returning. The commit message explicitly states: "In the event that rpcrdma_post_recvs() fails to create a work request (due to memory allocation failure, say) or otherwise exits early, we should decrement ep->re_receiving before returning. Otherwise we will hang in rpcrdma_xprt_drain() as re_receiving will never reach zero." The fix references commit 15788d1d1077 which introduced the `re_receiving` counter mechanism, indicating the decrement logic was missing from the original implementation.
